study: Lower the desk's price floor from $10 to $2 in a replay of the live desk, and short what it buys under $10 with the live exits mirrored. Do the small momentum names the desk would have bought fall after its entry by more than they cost to short?
registered_at: 2026-10-19, before any replay of this arm was run.
origin: Operator 2026-10-19, after fill_short was written: 'It would also allow us to use the momentum stocks, the smaller ones the floor lowered to two dollars' and 'Testing sub-$10 names the desk never bought would need a separate replay with the price floor lowered. I want this tested too.' The desk's real fills are $10+ (ai_watch_min_price 10), so fill_short cannot answer this.
prior_evidence: Stated before the run. SHORT_SQUARES_2026-10-02 (all names, the square signal, tier costs 0.40% for $5-10 and 1.00% under $5): every cell negative; the squeeze tail on all names p99 +18.9%, max +224% in 30 minutes. short_fade_study (2026-09-25): admitted names, a coin flip that failed held out with a p99 +90% squeeze. Expected: under $10 the measured spread is several times the $10+ spread and a net loss is likely.
replay: scripts/floor2_sweep.sh: tools/replay_session.py on the recorded sessions 2026-10-06, 07, 08, 09, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16 (the turn_open set), pinned to the whole live config of the commit (--set-json), with only these changed: ai_watch_profile_path empty (as every sweep), ai_watch_min_price, ai_watch_momentum_min_price, ai_watch_movers_min_price, ai_tight_min_price, rs_min_price and h4_min_price all 2.0, and ai_max_positions 20 with ai_max_position_pct 5 (more seats, so more of the desk's small-name buy decisions are taken; turn_open's turn20 sizing). Every other gate stays as live: spread, RVOL, stale quote, the cheap band (ai_watch_cheap_price 5, ai_max_position_pct_cheap 5), source rules, the arm lanes. Names live never watched get the replay's synthetic engine rows (SIP 1-minute bars, last completed close, true age; cap 50, the Finnhub limit); those opens are flagged synthetic and counted. Only names on the RECORDED source lists can be seated: a source whose recorded list was already cut at $10 contributes no small names; per-tier counts and names are printed.
population: Every replay open (closed list, any exit) on the floor2 arm, any price. The replay's own fill price and exit are not used: each open's decision time is a 'fill' handed to fill_short's scorer.
trade: As fill_short_prereg (and its amendment): short at the first SIP round-lot print within 120 s after the replay's decision time; covered by the desk's live exit code on the mirrored path (stop above, trail and ratchet on the low, trail_dc on mirrored completed bars, the double check on completed bars, the T1 blend, dead trade, 15:50 flatten); cover at the first real print after the decision.
cost: As fill_short: the full SIP quoted spread at the entry, charged once (no NBBO -> that day's pooled median, counted), plus 0.5 bp fees; borrow 0 for easy-to-borrow intraday. Printed besides: the 7 bp stop-slippage line and the tier round-trip cost line (0.40% $5-10, 1.00% $2-5).

sets.primary: entry print $2.00-$9.99, Alpaca shortable AND easy_to_borrow (today's flags), SSR known and off at entry.
sets.information: $2-5 and $5-10 separately; the $10+ opens of the same replay; hard to borrow, not shortable, SSR and SSR-unknown rows; synthetic-row opens; the long control (the same opens long through the unmirrored exits).

call: On the primary set, per-day mean net per trade, day-clustered. PASS: mean > 0 in half A and in half B; pooled t >= 2; the 7 bp line pooled > 0; pooled > 0 without the 3 best days; and the tier-cost line pooled > 0. PROMISING: > 0 in both halves and pooled t >= 1.5. FAIL otherwise. UNDERPOWERED: fewer than 8 scored days, fewer than 4 in either half, or fewer than 100 primary trades. NOT READ: asset flags unknown for more than 25% of the $2-10 rows, fetch errors above 5% of attempted opens, or any replay day failed.
known_limits: The replay is a model of the desk (its live arm opened 13-69 a day where the desk filled 21-98 on these days). Sub-$10 names come only from recorded lists that kept them. Asset flags are today's. Locates, short rejections, the SSR uptick rule's effect on the fill (only its presence is checked) and halts (LULD) are not modelled; small names halt often, and a halted short cannot be covered. 20 seats is wider than live. SIP-only prices. Nine sessions.
no_retuning: The floor (2.0), the seats, the sessions, the halves, the scorer and the costs are fixed. Another floor, size, session set or filter is a new prereg. A PASS earns a forward paper period on the short side, never money directly.
command: On the mini after 16:15 ET (or with SWEEP_DAYTIME=1 and the data-only account): nohup bash scripts/floor2_sweep.sh /tmp/floor2_DATE > /tmp/floor2_run.log 2>&1 &. It ends by running TH_DATA_SECRETS=... .venv/bin/python tools/studies/fill_short.py --replay-dir /tmp/floor2_DATE.
amendment_2026-10-19: Result-skeptic Mode 1 NOT READY, before any replay or return; changed: (1) Alpaca allows short sales under $5 but the maintenance margin is the greater of $2.50/share or 100% of value (docs.alpaca.markets margin-and-short-selling), so a $2-5 short ties up 100-125% of its value in buying power; the per-trade return is unchanged, the number of such shorts an account can hold is not; recorded as a known limit, primary still starts at $2.00 with Alpaca's shortable and easy_to_borrow flags; (2) PASS also needs the pooled day mean > 0 without the 5 names with the largest total net; (3) the replay's open_at_end positions are scored too; (4) the scorer exits with the replay's pinned base_config.json (the commit's whole config), not the mini's current file; (5) the primary set's synthetic-row share is printed; (6) SWEEP_PROBE=1 replays 2026-10-06 only and prints its opens by tier and synthetic flag, with no returns, run before the full sweep to see whether small names reach the book at all; (7) known limits added: the sweep runs without --live-staleness, as turn_open did, and the replay without it opens about 4x as often as live on stale tape; tight_stocks.json is cut at $10 by its producer, so of the files checked only movers_stocks.json can carry $2-10 names (research, Trader Bro, trending and the dashboard momentum lists unchecked; tools/studies/floor2_check.py counts them per recorded file).
